title: The Bigger Picture — Daily AI Analysis
paragraphs: A deeper look at today's Bigger Picture card: what is moving the market, and what to watch. The Full Report carries the full analysis.

What moves the market today. Fact: Reuters reports that Tuesday brought the heaviest selling of AI supplier shares since late July: South Korea's main index fell more than 6 percent on a fifth day of chipmaker losses and the main US chip index headed for a sixth straight fall, on worries that rising interest rates could derail the boom; Marc Velan, head of investments at Lucerne Asset Management in Singapore, blames positioning and the cost of capital, not demand. CGTN reports that the International Monetary Fund's World Economic Outlook names the possible end of the AI investment boom among the main risks and says a steep fall in AI investment could cut US output by 1.8 percent by 2028.

Fact: Reuters reports that ASML, the Dutch maker of chip-making machines, said on Wednesday it cannot fully meet AI-driven demand in 2027 and 2028. Bloomberg reports that Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive of Meta, said Meta committed hundreds of billions of dollars to AI before knowing whether it would pay off. Semafor reports that Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said AI-boom price rises are spreading beyond data-centre supplies and may be plain overheating. Reuters reports, citing two people with direct knowledge, that AirTrunk, Blackstone's data-centre operator, postponed a 1.5 billion dollar Singapore listing in the sell-off.

Our view: ASML cannot fully meet demand for its chip-making machines in 2027 and 2028, yet chip shares fell for a fifth day in Seoul and the main US chip index headed for a sixth straight fall; both can be true only if the market is selling the price of the next quarter, not the demand. The Fund has put a number on a fall and a Fed president has tied the boom to inflation, so interest rates are the hinge of the AI trade.

What to watch and follow. 1. Thursday 15 October: TSMC's third-quarter results, from its own investor page; after ASML, the second supplier to say how far demand runs, and a raised outlook says supply is still the limit. 2. Wednesday 21 October: Meta's results, from Meta's own notice, the first of the four big spenders to report. 3. 27 to 28 October: the Federal Reserve meets, from its own calendar, and Alphabet and Microsoft report on 28 October, from their own investor pages; the Fed sets the cost of the build's borrowing. 4. 2 November: shareholders vote on the merger that would list Agility Robotics, from Agility's own release, which Agility says would make it the only US-listed pure-play humanoid robot maker with commercial deployments. SK hynix's 27 October and Samsung's 29 October are reported, not confirmed by the companies.

Unknowns. How much of Korea's fall is foreign selling; the figures Anthropic is reported to show institutional investors today; whether Microsoft's reported Azure cost cuts, which it disputes, are real; and whether the September US inflation figure comes on 14 October, which the statistics bureau's own page does not list.
This is analysis of the news, not financial advice or an investment recommendation.
